content:
Let \(c=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}\).

First inequality:
\[
\frac{2n+1}{3n+8}<c \iff 2n+1<c(3n+8)
\]
\[
\iff (2-3c)n<8c-1
\]
Since \(2-3c>0\),
\[
n<\frac{8c-1}{2-3c}=\frac{13\sqrt5+25}{2}.
\]

Second inequality:
\[
c<\frac{n+7}{2n+1}\iff c(2n+1)<n+7
\]
\[
\iff (2c-1)n<7-c
\]
Since \(2c-1>0\),
\[
n<\frac{7-c}{2c-1}=\frac{13\sqrt5+25}{2}.
\]

Thus both hold exactly when
\[
n<\frac{13\sqrt5+25}{2}\approx 27.034.
\]
The largest positive integer satisfying this is \(27\).

\[
\boxed{27}
\]
